messages:
alex: :rotating_light: alert — seeing a sustained fanout spike against inference in us-west-2. tail latency up, a few customers report 429s. traffic profile: a small set of routes (/v1/batch, /v1/generate) with high token/sec, concentrated in ~3 ASNs and ~10k ephemeral IPs. starting triage.

sophie: grabbing graphs now. token/sec is ~4x baseline, batch endpoints look worst. some spikes align with specific UA strings.

daniel: prelim check of edge logs shows repeated identical prompt prefixes and fast-retry patterns — looks automated. i'll prepare a WAF signature and ASN blocks.

irene: eta on mitigations? CS is already getting pings from customers. suggest we prepare a short customer note and reduce quotas for noisy accounts.

alex: executing quick mitigations: preparing WAF rule and soft rate limits. plan: 1) WAF sig match for bot fingerprint + block top abusive ASN, 2) per-IP rate limits on heavy routes, 3) temporary quota throttle for accounts exceeding threshold, 4) disable anonymous batch uploads for 15m if needed.

pd-bot: PagerDuty: Incident P12345 assigned to alex

incident-bot: oncall assignment request: alex is on-call. Hand-off suggestion to @sophie?

sophie: i will take the incident and coordinate live mitigation. moving control to me.

daniel: pushing WAF rule id=90012 to edge (match: UA regex + payload entropy). command we ran: 
```
# wafctl
wafctl add-rule --id 90012 --action block --match-ua ".*(python-requests|curl|httpx).*" --match-entropy > 0.6
```
Blocked top ASN 39456 and 45321 via edge ACL (rule applied to us-west-2).

alex: also applying quick per-route rate limits:
```
redwood-cli routes update --route /v1/batch --rate-limit 60rpm --scope per-ip
redwood-cli routes update --route /v1/generate --rate-limit 120rpm --scope per-ip
```
This should reduce abusive fanout while preserving legitimate interactive traffic.

irene: sending CS draft to affected accounts: 
"We observed abnormal automated traffic impacting latency. We've applied temporary rate limits and edge protections. Expect recovery within 10-20 minutes. If you continue to see 429s, reply here and we will prioritize."

sophie: monitoring dashboards — 65% of offending traffic now dropped by WAF/ACL. overall 5xxs down, user-visible 429s reduced but a couple of enterprise customers still report errors.

daniel: adding a fallback shaping policy that backs off aggressive clients rather than hard-blocking. deployed rule: token-bucket per-customer with exponential backoff on retries.

alex: important operational note: do NOT broadly blackhole the ASN ranges for now — that risks collateral. keep blocks tied to signature matches and rate-limits for IP-level traffic.

sophie: enabled additional request header capture (anonymized) for top 100 offending IPs to help postmortem. starting a small canary of mitigations to verify no false positives.

daniel: warming KV cache for popular prefixes to reduce repeated token generation costs. that shaving reduced token/sec by ~10%.

irene: CS updated customers and opened support tickets for the ones who reported errors. they'll update if any customer needs escalation.

sophie: handoff planned at 1764123798 — i'll step out and hand primary back to alex for the next 2h. postmortem owner will be me, WAF/edge owner daniel, customer comms owner irene.

alex: taking over. next actions: gather top-50 offending IPs + UA strings, export WAF hits, create repeating-pattern alert for 24h, schedule postmortem doc and link to this thread.

irene: note for CS: "Mitigations are live; we will follow up with a postmortem and remediation plan. Tickets will be updated as we learn more."

pd-bot: Incident P12345 status updated: mitigated -> monitoring

sophie: :white_check_mark: traffic improving and mitigations look effective. opening postmortem doc now and will link artifacts (waf logs, top-ip list, graphs). closing live thread but leaving follow-ups in the PM doc."
